title: The Overtime Tax Illusion
hook_text: WORKING OVERTIME JUST COST YOU MONEY

beats.say: Working that extra 10-hour shift feels like a win, until you run the actual tax math.
beats.visual: A close-up of hands reviewing a glowing pay stub on a dark wooden desk under a single desk lamp.

beats.say: That bonus cash pushes your total earnings right into a higher marginal tax bracket.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a worker staring out a rainy office window at night.

beats.say: So why does working more hours suddenly yield less than minimum wage take-home pay?
beats.visual: A stack of coins sitting beside a calculator in dim morning light.

beats.say: Most people assume every extra dollar earned keeps the exact same tax rate.
beats.visual: A close-up of a pen tapping slowly on a blank notepad.

beats.say: The truth is, federal and state withholdings jump the second you cross the threshold.
beats.visual: A blurred shot of a city skyline at dusk through a car windshield.

beats.say: When payroll taxes and higher brackets combine, what happens to your hourly bonus?
beats.visual: A person counting cash bills at a kitchen table, shot from overhead.

beats.say: Your net take-home pay on those extra hours plummets below your base rate.
beats.visual: A close-up of a digital clock ticking past midnight in a quiet room.

beats.say: How much of your hard work actually ends up in your bank account?
beats.visual: An open leather wallet resting on a cold concrete surface.

beats.say: After all deductions, you might bring home less than $5 an hour for that shift.
beats.visual: A single coin resting on top of a stack of tax forms.

beats.say: That is the hidden tax math behind every extra shift you pick up.
beats.visual: A hand closing a laptop lid in a dark room.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A silhouette walking down a quiet hallway toward an open door with warm light.

caption: Working overtime doesn't always pay like you think. Check the tax math before your next extra shift. #Overtime #TaxMath #PersonalFinance #MoneyTips #QuietMoney
description: Discover how marginal tax brackets turn extra work hours into lower take-home pay than you expect.
first_comment: Have you ever checked your effective hourly rate after tax on an overtime shift?

facts.claim: Marginal tax brackets can reduce the effective take-home pay of overtime hours significantly due to combined federal, state, and payroll withholdings.
facts.basis: Standard progressive tax bracket mechanics in payroll systems.

loop_map.stakes: Working extra overtime shifts for more take-home pay.
